newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: German Mueller eats into Austrian bread market.
newsitem.headline: German Mueller eats into Austrian bread market.

text.p: Bavarian baker Mueller-Brot has become the latest German firm to gain a foothold in Austrian retailing, taking a majority stake in the Alpine Republic's biggest and most traditional baker Ankerbrot.

Helmut Schuster, Anker's majority owner since 1981, confirmed late on Wednesday that he had agreed to sell the bulk of his shares to family-run Mueller, retaining only a blocking minority. He gave no further details.
"This is in response to a changing market situation - an extended Europe and Austria's entry into the European Union," the Vienna-based firm said in a statement.

Founded in 1891 and former purveyor to the Habsburg court, Anker employs 3,000 staff and has 349 outlets. It supplies daily bread to at least a third of Viennese and has a national market share of more than 50 percent.
Mueller has 300 shops and employs 2,000 staff.
Mueller boss Hans Mueller junior assured Anker staff on Thursday that the new regime would not endanger existing jobs but he declined to guarantee there would be no shop closures.
"Jobs will be more secure than they would be if Anker remained independent," Mueller told Austrian radio.
Last year, Germany's Rewe took Austrian retail by storm when it snapped up the country's biggest supermarket chain Billa for an estimated 15 billion schillings ($1.3 billion).

Mueller declined to give any financial details of his company's acquisition, which is subject to cartel authority approval. In September, Anker announced Mueller had acquired five percent of its preferred shares and the two firms had launched a cross-border cooperation.
Anker has a base capital of 100 million schillings, of which 66.6 million is in Schuster's hands. The firm has said it expects to breakeven in 1996 with sales of 2.9 billion schillings.
Mueller posted sales of 360 million marks (2.5 billion schillings) in 1996.
Anker preferred shares, which are listed on the Vienna stock exchange's secondary market, closed at 475 schillings on Wednesday.
-- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-254 ($ = 11.61 Austrian Schillings)
